memos.headline: S08 and S09 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S02 and S01 Remain Broken
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe. S08 is the cleanest chart: only 1% off its 52-week high, +6.4% above its 50d mean, +20.9% above its 200d mean, RSI 64.8 (strong but not overbought), and 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +15.4%. S09 is a close second with just a 2.2% drawdown, solid 4w rel strength of +5.1%, and low ATR of 1.74% making it a lower-vol trend ride. S05 and S07 have spectacular 26-week returns (+74.4% and +61.7%) and massive relative strength, but both sit 40%+ above their 200d means—I respect the trend but the extension makes me less confident in fresh entries here. On the other side, S02 is in a structural downtrend: -47.3% drawdown from highs, -14.5% below its 200d mean, RSI 37.4, and 4-week relative strength of -10.9%—this is a name to avoid until it reclaims its 50d mean. S01 is similarly weak at -17.8% drawdown, -7.7% below its 200d, and persistent negative relative strength.

views.note: Strongest risk-adjusted trend in the universe: only 1% off highs, RSI 64.8, +6.4% above 50d—would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~256).
Near highs with 2.2% drawdown, low ATR 1.74%, and positive 4w/12w relative strength; a close below the 50d mean (~114) would change my view.
Massive 12w +38.4% move and +32.7% rel strength vs SPY, but +40.3% above 200d mean raises reversion risk; would trim on a break below 260.
Trend is undeniable (+61.7% in 26w) but +38.9% above 200d mean and 3.91% ATR make chasing risky; need a pullback toward the 50d to get involved.
Sitting right at its 50d mean with RSI 47.4 and negative 12w relative strength of -4.5%; no edge either way until it breaks above 540 or below 480.
RSI 44.4 and -1.3% below 50d suggest fading momentum; flat relative strength gives no reason to be involved until a clear direction emerges.
Sharp -4.0% last week after a +10.2% 4w run looks like a failed breakout attempt; 12w rel strength vs SPY is flat at 0.0%.
Strong 26w return of +54.6% but 8.1% drawdown and 4.72% ATR with middling RSI 49.4 suggest consolidation; wait for a move above 200 to re-engage.
Persistent downtrend: -17.8% drawdown, -7.7% below 200d mean, -12.7% 12w rel strength vs SPY; would need a reclaim of the 200d mean (~160) to reconsider.
Worst chart in the universe: -47.3% drawdown, -14.5% below 200d mean, RSI 37.4, and accelerating 4w relative weakness of -10.9%; stay away until price reclaims the 50d mean (~348).

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Superior Earnings Power; S02 Margin Collapse Is a Red Flag
memos.body: I screened the latest filings across the universe and the dispersion in earnings quality is striking. S10 stands out with 56.5% net margins, +55.6% YoY revenue growth, and minimal debt ($8.47B), making it the cleanest earnings compounder in the group. S05 is also compelling at 34.2% net margins with +33% net income growth and only $14.79B in debt. On the other end, S02 posted a 2.1% net margin on $113B of revenue with net income down 61.2% YoY despite 12.2% top-line growth—classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for. S09 is also deteriorating with revenue declining 5.2% and net income falling 12.3%, while carrying $32.8B in debt. I would need to see margin stabilization in S02 and a return to revenue growth in S09 before reconsidering either name.

views.note: 56.5% net margin, +55.6% revenue growth, and only $8.47B debt represent the best earnings power and balance sheet in the universe.
34.2% net margin with +33% net income growth on low leverage ($14.79B debt) signals durable, high-quality earnings.
35.7% net margin and +18.4% revenue growth are strong, though +12.5% net income growth lags the top line slightly, warranting monitoring of cost trends.
Revenue of $180B growing 13.4% is impressive but 11.8% net margin is thin for the scale; I need to see margin expansion before getting constructive.
Net income surged 86.4% YoY to $27.5B but $90.68B in total debt and only 7.9% revenue growth temper enthusiasm; debt trajectory is the key variable.
Solid 21.2% net margin and +20% net income growth, but only 3% revenue growth suggests limited top-line momentum.
31% net margin is healthy but $427B in total debt dwarfs the rest of the universe; leverage is the swing factor.
Revenue declining 5.2% with net income down 12.3% and $32.8B in debt signals deteriorating earnings power; would reconsider on a return to top-line growth.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to just $2.35B on $113B revenue (2.1% margin) despite double-digit revenue growth—textbook cash-flow compression.
9.5% revenue growth is decent but net income fell 6.7% and 13% margins with $31.7B debt leave little margin of safety.

memos.headline: Fed in Easing Mode but Sticky 3% CPI and Rising Unemployment Signal a Cautious Late-Cycle Regime
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing cycle — the upper bound has dropped 75bp over the past year to 4.00%, with 50bp of that in the last three months alone. However, headline CPI is running at 3.0% y/y (Sep print), which is still uncomfortably above target and limits the pace of further cuts. The labor market is softening meaningfully, with unemployment at 4.40%, up 30bp over both three- and twelve-month horizons, consistent with a late-cycle slowdown. The 10y-2y spread has re-steepened +36bp y/y to +0.53pp, confirming the market is pricing in continued easing, while the 10y yield at 4.14% has drifted lower but remains elevated enough to pressure rate-sensitive sectors. A CPI print breaking convincingly below 2.5% or unemployment spiking above 4.7% would shift my regime call toward aggressive easing, favoring duration and growth more decisively.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from the easing cycle and falling 10y yields (-29bp y/y), though sticky CPI caps upside.
Banks face a flattening NIM as the front end falls faster than the long end, but the positive 10y-2y spread of 53bp provides some cushion.
Staples are attractive in a late-cycle slowdown with unemployment rising 30bp and the Fed still cutting; defensive positioning warranted.
Cyclicals face headwinds from rising unemployment and a decelerating economy; the labor market deterioration argues against pro-cyclical exposure.
Energy lacks a clear macro catalyst — easing helps demand expectations but 3% CPI and softening growth create offsetting forces.
Rate-sensitive sectors benefit as the 10y yield drops and the Fed continues easing, though conviction is moderate given sticky inflation.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S07 and S03 Surge While S04 and S06 Face Negative Reactions
memos.body: I am seeing a clear bifurcation in earnings-season sentiment across the universe. S07 posted an extraordinary +11.6% price reaction on its 10/29 results and S03 followed with +9.6% on 10/30, signaling strong positive narrative shifts that may still have momentum given the magnitude of the moves. On the other side, S04 dropped -2.9% on its 10/29 earnings release and S06 fell -1.9% on its 10/14 report, both suggesting disappointed expectations and potentially souring tone. S08, S09, S01, and S02 all printed near-flat reactions (ranging from -0.4% to +0.5%), which I read as already-priced narratives with no clear directional signal from sentiment alone. I have highest conviction on the positive inflection names where the magnitude of the reaction suggests a genuine narrative shift rather than noise.

views.note: The +11.6% earnings-day reaction is the strongest in the universe and signals a major positive narrative shift that likely has follow-through.
A +9.6% post-earnings move indicates a decisive positive sentiment inflection that may not yet be fully absorbed by the market.
The -2.9% earnings reaction combined with a recent director change suggests negative tone building; sentiment headwinds likely persist near-term.
A -1.9% earnings reaction on 10/14 and subsequent Other Events filing on 10/22 suggest lingering negative sentiment without a clear catalyst for reversal.
Near-flat -0.4% earnings reaction suggests the market had already priced in the result; no directional sentiment signal.
A muted +0.2% earnings reaction and high filing volume (six 8-Ks in a month) suggest noise rather than a clear narrative shift.
The +0.5% earnings reaction is negligible; subsequent Reg FD and bylaws amendments are procedural and do not shift sentiment.
A -0.3% earnings reaction is essentially flat; the director change and Other Events filing add noise but no clear tone direction.
A +2.5% earnings reaction is modestly positive and the follow-on Other Events filing on 11/6 may sustain constructive tone, though conviction is lower than S07/S03.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Near Doubling in 3 Months Signals Structural Geopolitical Risk Repricing Across the Universe
memos.body: I am flagging a dramatic surge in the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index, which at 476 has nearly doubled over three months (+97.3%) and risen 18.6% in the last month alone—this is a structural shift, not a one-quarter event. VIX at 20.00 is up 38% over three months, confirming that markets are pricing elevated tail risk, likely tied to escalating trade/sanctions policy and energy security concerns. WTI crude at $59.54 is down 6.5% over three months, which is unusual alongside rising geopolitical uncertainty and suggests demand-side weakness or supply normalization that could reverse sharply on any energy-security shock. High-yield OAS at 3.09% remains relatively contained (only +19bp over 3 months), so credit markets are not yet in distress, but the gap between policy uncertainty and credit spreads is historically unstable. I would need to see a de-escalation in export controls or sanctions rhetoric—or a sustained drop in the EPU index below 350—to change my cautious posture on names with significant geopolitical exposure.

views.note: Heavy 8-K filing cadence (four filings in a month) suggests active corporate developments, but without content detail I cannot determine geopolitical exposure direction amid surging policy uncertainty.

Three 8-K filings including a very recent 8.01 on Nov 13 warrant monitoring, but the near-doubling of policy uncertainty makes me reluctant to take a directional view without clarity on supply-chain or sanctions exposure.
Two 8-K filings in October amid a policy uncertainty environment that has nearly doubled suggest elevated headline risk; I prefer to stay away until the EPU index stabilizes below 400.
Single 8.01 filing on Nov 6 provides limited signal; with VIX up 38% over three months and policy uncertainty surging, I lack conviction to go either direction.
Recent Reg FD disclosure on Nov 7 is noted but insufficient to form a geopolitical view; the benign HY OAS at 3.09% provides some comfort but policy uncertainty at 476 keeps me sidelined.

With WTI crude down 6.5% over three months yet policy uncertainty nearly doubling, any energy-exposed or trade-sensitive name like S04 faces asymmetric downside risk from a sanctions or export-control escalation.
